text:
Alice Park: Heads-up — run into a weird edge case in the private endpoint cutover spike. When we flip routing from regional relay -> per-customer endpoint some customers see 502s during cert rotation.
Ben Cho: Hmm, 502s during cert rotation? Is that TLS termination moving at the relay or the endpoint?
Alice Park: Endpoint terminates TLS now. Relay used to. During rollout we observed an interplay between short-lived controlplane connections and client retries that leaks into upstreams.
Carol Nguyen: Any logs? example request/trace ids?
Alice Park: Sent to #eng-sre but quick snippet here: ``[proxy] upstream reset after 2s TLS handshake error: certificate not yet valid``. Happens ~10s after we update endpoint certs.
David Patel: Could be time skew on the agent machines or stale certs in the relay connection pool. Are agents doing keepalive reuse?
Alice Park: Yes, agents keep connections pooled to reduce latency. Pool doesn't detect new cert until recycle.
Ben Cho: Two quick options: 1) ensure zero-downtime cert reload path (graceful drain + new handshake) or 2) orchestrate cutover that avoids simultaneous controlplane -> data path cert changes.
Carol Nguyen: For (1) we need connection draining hooks in the agent and probably a new healthcheck that waits for pool refresh. That is a medium-sized infra change.
David Patel: For (2) we can do staged cutover: create new endpoint with new cert, update routing to point to new endpoint, then deprecate old. But per-customer endpoints blow up DNS counts and route churn.
Ben Cho: Also add: routing needs to survive transient DNS TTLs and duplication across regions. We saw breakage when clients used cached IPs.
Alice Park: Client caching is the root cause for some customers (mobile SDKs + NAT). They keep old IP and hit relay which no longer accepts the client cert.
infra-bot: Deploy bot: rollout started for customer-cp-cutover v2 -> 3 at 2025-11-02T15:12:04Z
Carol Nguyen: Another idea: keep TLS termination at relay but forward authenticated connection (mTLS) to endpoint over private peering. That keeps client-facing surface stable while controlplane/endpoint cert rotation happens behind the relay.
David Patel: That adds operational burden (relay must maintain customer certs & mapping) and weakens the per-customer isolation guarantee. Tradeoff: operational complexity vs rollback simplicity.
Ben Cho: Could we implement a hybrid: relay continues to terminate for short TTL after cutover and acts as a TCP-level pass-through once endpoint certs are validated? Something like a phased downgrade.
Alice Park: Phased approach sounds promising. Steps I'm thinking: 1) provision per-customer endpoint with new certs but keep relay target active, 2) warm pipeline and do healthchecks against endpoint, 3) flip client DNS to new endpoint IPs with low TTL, 4) keep relay in passthrough mode for 2m for retries, 5) drain relay connections and remove mapping.
Carol Nguyen: We need to instrument per-route metrics: handshake errors, connection reuse age, and DNS miss rate. Otherwise we won't detect the reason quickly.
David Patel: Agreed. Also add a kill-switch: immediate rollback to relay-only routing via operator-run script. Make sure we can inject a header to force passthrough on a per-customer basis for debugging.
Alice Park: I'll draft a cutover checklist with exact timeouts and commands. Quick ask: can Platform Ops add a fast rollback job in the operator that toggles routing and forces agent pool recycle?
Ben Cho: Yes, we can add an operator job. Need to be careful with rate limits on route updates. We'll batch by region/cust group of 50.
Carol Nguyen: One more SRE ask: add a cert-rotation simulator in staging that exercises connection pools, client caching, and partial DNS flips. This will help avoid surprises.
Alice Park: Great. I'll put a short RFC follow-up with the proposed phased cutover and rollback steps. Will ping for review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
David Patel: Thanks — and log the exact failure traces to the onboard incident so we can correlate with canary customers.
infra-bot: Incident bot: new incident created #INC-20251102-73 "endpoint-cutover-502s" assigned to eng-sre
Ben Cho: Also note: document that any future design that moves TLS termination must consider agent pool lifecycle and client-side caching. Small TTLs aren't enough for mobile.
Carol Nguyen: +1. Also add note about customer expectations around isolation during the transitional window.
Alice Park: Copy. Will include all those in the RFC follow-up and schedule a short sync with Ops and SRE tomorrow at 10:00.
